extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, patent practitioners, inventors, and stakeholders in patent law (industry, universities, unions)
extracted.subtask_description: Legislative debate and commentary on H.R. 1908 (Patent Reform Act of 2007) focusing on best-mode, post-grant review scope, damages determination, and patent-quality/system improvements. The page records arguments, proposed amendment text, and cited empirical/legal guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best mode specification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications must "set forth the best mode contemplated by the inventor of carrying out his invention" at the time the application is filed (the traditional 'best mode' requirement contained in section 112).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Pence amendment (and discussion) emphasizes keeping best mode as a specification requirement for obtaining a patent (i.e., applicants should disclose their best mode in the filing). The page notes that best mode is a uniquely U.S. requirement (not required in Europe or Japan) and that it historically imposes a subjective duty on applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude best mode from post-grant review and litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments about best mode should not serve as a basis for post-grant review proceedings or be litigated as a defense to patent enforceability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pence's amendment seeks to 'remove best mode from litigation' while retaining it as an Office filing requirement — i.e., keep best mode in the Patent Office but prevent it from being a ground in post-grant review or a satellite litigation issue. Rationale: eliminates costly, subjective litigation over best mode and reduces defensive legal expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent quality: strong, high-quality patents and reduced lawsuit abuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent law reform should produce 'strong and high quality' patents while also eliminating 'lawsuit abuse' that burdens inventors and the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed means include updating laws for the 21st century and reforms targeted at reducing abusive litigation. Opponents counter that improving Patent Office resourcing (more examiners, training, retaining user fees to improve operations) would better address bad patents than wholesale rule changes. Use empirical measures of patent quality and targeted Patent Office improvements when evaluating reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages determination principles (apportionment, burden, and complexity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Damages provisions should respect established damages law (e.g., Georgia-Pacific factors, apportionment rules, Entire Market Value Rule) and clearly assign burdens of proof; they should not force a massive macroeconomic analysis in every case or create undue complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited guidance from the Chief Judge of the Federal Circuit (Paul R. Michel) and other experienced litigators: (1) under current caselaw the burden of apportioning the base for reasonable royalties falls on the infringer while the burden for the Entire Market Value Rule falls on the patentee; (2) the bill's proposed changes risk requiring a massive damages trial in every case without assigning burdens or standards of proof; (3) ambiguous statutory phrases would be litigated for years causing uncertainty and increased costs; (4) any statutory reform should carefully craft burden assignments and standards so as not to disrupt settled case law and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do empirical study of damages before major legal change
rubrics_metrics.description: Before enacting sweeping changes to damages law, Congress should study patent damage awards (e.g., from at least 1990 to present) to understand actual effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mr. Manzullo and others argued for having study results available prior to making 'massive change in law'; the page records calls to study damages historically rather than passing reforms first and studying later. This is a procedural/evidence-based criterion for policymaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit scope of post-grant review to avoid satellite issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-grant review procedural scope should be circumscribed so it does not become a vehicle for collateral, costly disputes (e.g., best mode claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Pence amendment is cited as clarifying that best mode cannot be raised in post-grant review. The underlying guidance is that post-grant review should focus on core patentability/validity issues rather than ancillary, subjective specification issues that generate separate litigation tracks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use empirical litigation incidence when assessing need for reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Reform decisions should take into account that only a small percentage of granted patents lead to lawsuits (table showing ~1.47% in 2006 and similar rates across years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ms. Kaptur and others point to USPTO and Federal Judicial Statistics (patents granted vs. suits commenced) to argue that litigation is a minuscule percent of patents and that sweeping changes may be unnecessary. Policy evaluation should weigh such empirical incidence rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative process standards: adequate deliberation and opportunity for amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Major changes to patent law should not be 'amended on the run' on the floor; they should undergo committee consideration, ample hearings, stakeholder negotiation, and not be rushed under limited debate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several speakers urge sending the bill back to committee if there remain substantial unresolved objections, noting that rapid floor amendments and limited debate undermine the process. This is a procedural standard for producing durable, defensible patent law reforms.
